name: BYD Company Limited (比亚迪股份有限公司)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: BYD is the world's largest BESS system integrator by H1 2026 shipments on two independent counts (Benchmark 9.1%, InfoLink #1) and fourth in cells, while its group result went the other way — H1 2026 revenue RMB 344.82B (-7.13%) and net profit RMB 12.33B (-20.54%) against a peer set whose listed Chinese BESS players all grew profit sharply. Storage is not separately disclosed and sits inside an automotive P&L compressed by the domestic price war, so the storage business is visible only in third-party shipment counts and in the order book: 11.275 GWh for Masdar, 12.5 GWh for Saudi Electricity Company, 2.4 GWh for Greenvolt in Poland. BACKGROUND: BYD is a Chinese conglomerate spanning batteries, new-energy vehicles, electronics, and rail transit, and one of the world's largest battery-energy-storage suppliers. Its storage arm — the Energy Storage & New-type Battery Business Division (BYD Energy Storage, est. 2008), supplied by cell subsidiary FinDreams Battery — makes LFP 'Blade' cells and integrated BESS products from grid-scale containers to home batteries. BYD is also China's largest NEV maker (4.60M NEVs sold in 2025, >1M exported), sharing the Blade LFP platform between vehicles and storage.
ecosystemRole: We assess BYD as top-tier in every storage ranking, with scope-dependent placement: #2 global ESS battery shipper in 2023 (28.4 GWh, Fastmarkets), #3 ESS cell shipper in 2024 (SMM/InfoLink), and for 2025 Benchmark ranked BYD the #1 global BESS system integrator (~60 GWh, 13% share, overtaking Tesla) while InfoLink placed it #3 in systems — estimates differ by scope. Company-reported: >75 GWh in commercial operation across 360+ projects in 110+ countries by end-2024. FinDreams capacity expansion (incl. Chongqing blade-cell base and Wuwei, Gansu) took planned battery capacity above 500 GWh in 2025.

productsAndServices.name: HaoHan utility-scale platform (浩瀚, flagship 2025–)
productsAndServices.description: Launched September 18, 2025 at the International Digital Energy Expo (Shenzhen): the world's largest single-unit DC block at 14.5 MWh — more than double the 6–7 MWh industry norm — built on a 2,710 Ah long Blade LFP cell (claimed >300% single-cell capacity gain vs earlier generations, −30°C to 55°C operation). A 20-ft-container configuration delivers 10 MWh at 233 kWh/m³ volumetric density (+51% vs industry average). Sold as a platform with the GC Flux grid-forming PCS (2.5–10 MW) and GC Master EMS. Deployed at gigawatt scale from late 2025.
highlights: 11.275 GWh HaoHan supply contract signed July 2026 for Masdar/EWEC's 5.2 GW / 19 GWh round-the-clock solar-plus-storage project in Abu Dhabi — the world's first gigascale RTC renewable project, online from 2027
Claimed lifecycle energy cost below CNY 0.1/kWh (~$0.014/kWh) and >10,000 cycles
productsAndServices.positioning: Single-block capacity leadership: 14.5 MWh vs CATL TENER's 6.25 MWh (9 MWh TENER Stack announced) and Tesla Megapack 3's ~5 MWh per unit. BYD's pitch is fewer blocks, less land, and lower balance-of-plant per MWh, plus grid-forming capability bundled in-house (GC Flux) rather than via a third-party PCS vendor — competing head-on with Sungrow's PowerTitan integrated approach.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct framework supply agreements with utilities, sovereign developers, and IPPs (Masdar, Saudi Electricity Company); BYD supplies the DC block + PCS + EMS while EPC partners handle plant integration
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Gigawatt-scale grid-side storage, round-the-clock solar-plus-storage tenders, Middle East / Latin America / China utility programs
productsAndServices.roadmap: Liquid-cooling integration on the 2026 roadmap (launch version cooling unspecified); Masdar RTC deliveries run through 2027 COD

productsAndServices.name: MC Cube-T utility container (2024–)
productsAndServices.description: 6.432 MWh containerized system introduced April 2024, the first with CTS (cell-to-system) integration of BYD's new-generation long-blade storage cells — up to +11% single-cell energy and +35.8% system energy vs the prior MC Cube, with −24.7% footprint. Built from modular ~500 kWh units combined into enclosures up to 6.4+ MWh; GB/T 36276-compliant. The volume workhorse behind the Saudi Electricity Company and Grenergy Chile fleets.
highlights: 12.5 GWh SEC deal signed February 2025 (5 × 500 MW/2,500 MWh) — the world's largest grid-scale BESS award at signing, lifting SEC cooperation to 15.1 GWh

Grenergy Oasis de Atacama (Chile): 3 GWh across phases 1–3, +3.5 GWh phase 6 (624 MC Cube-T units, May 2025), +2.6 GWh for Central Oasis (March 2026) — Latin America's largest battery supply relationship
productsAndServices.positioning: Slightly above CATL TENER's 6.25 MWh per standard container and well above Tesla Megapack 3 (~5 MWh); differentiates on CTS integration density and BYD's vertically owned cell supply. In China's brutal per-kWh system pricing environment, BYD leans on cell self-supply cost rather than premium features.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct supply agreements with utilities and IPP/developers (SEC, Grenergy); repeat framework purchases are the norm
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility grid-side storage, large solar-plus-storage plants (Middle East, Latin America, China)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Planned ~BRL 500M ($98M) BESS assembly line in Brazil (module/pack/system integration, not cells) timed to Brazil's first large industrial storage auction in December 2026 — siting decision (Manaus vs new plant) pending

productsAndServices.name: MC Cube-SIB sodium-ion BESS (2024–)
productsAndServices.description: Claimed world's first high-performance sodium-ion BESS, announced November 2024: 2.3 MWh per 20-ft container using long-blade sodium-ion cells in the same CTS super-integrated design, 1,200 V nominal (800–1,400 V range). Trades much lower energy density (vs 5+ MWh LFP containers) for higher charge/discharge rates, wider operating temperature range, longer cycle life, and enhanced safety.
productsAndServices.positioning: A chemistry-hedge product against LFP incumbents and CATL's Naxtra sodium push — commercially niche today, aimed at duty cycles and climates where LFP degrades (high-rate cycling, extreme cold) and at lithium-price insurance
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same direct utility/developer channel as the LFP line
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Grid ancillary services, extreme-climate sites, customers hedging lithium exposure

productsAndServices.name: Storage cells — Blade LFP (FinDreams Battery)
productsAndServices.description: Dedicated storage cell family: 320 Ah thick-blade LFP cells (ceramic terminals, >10,000 cycles) for C&I products, and the 2,710 Ah long Blade cell powering HaoHan — roughly triple conventional storage-cell capacity, −30°C to 55°C. FinDreams also sells cells merchant: from Q1 2025 it supplies LFP cells to Tesla's Shanghai Megafactory, reportedly securing >20% of Megapack cell orders alongside primary supplier CATL. Benchmark ranked BYD #4 in 2025 global ESS cell shipments (~60 GWh, ~10%).
highlights: Merchant supply to Tesla Shanghai Megafactory (LFP storage cells, from Q1 2025) — BYD cells inside a direct competitor's flagship BESS product
productsAndServices.positioning: Vertical integration is the differentiator vs cell makers with no captive end-product demand (EVE, REPT BATTERO, Hithium): BYD consumes its own cells in vehicles and BESS at volumes that fund cost curves, then sells the surplus — competing with CATL both as cell merchant and as system vendor
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal transfer to BYD Energy Storage and BYD Auto; merchant cell sales to external OEMs/integrators (incl. Tesla)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Grid-scale and C&I storage integrators, EV/storage OEMs seeking non-CATL LFP supply

productsAndServices.name: C&I storage — Chess Plus (2025–)
productsAndServices.description: Modular AC-coupled C&I cabinet launched March 26, 2025 (Beijing Clean Energy Expo): China version 233 kWh / 125 kW at 729.6 V nominal, US version 350.1 kWh; scalable 125 kW–1 MW. Integrates BMS, distributed management control, EMS and AC unit in one enclosure with AI-driven O&M. Built on 320 Ah thick-blade cells with 2-hour fire-resistant battery casing and built-in aerosol suppression. Sold in China and the US; European version under evaluation.
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with Sungrow PowerStack, CATL EnerOne-derived cabinets, Sinexcel and Delta C&I offerings; leads with blade-cell safety story (fire-resistant casing, aerosol suppression, IP55, seismic rating) in a segment where thermal incidents drive procurement
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distribution/installer channel plus direct key accounts; regional product variants (CN fire-host / US smart-HVAC) tailored per market
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Factories, commercial buildings, EV-charging depots doing peak shaving, demand-charge management and backup
productsAndServices.roadmap: European variant under evaluation (as of 2025 launch); AI O&M feature expansion

productsAndServices.name: Residential storage — Battery-Box
productsAndServices.description: Modular LFP home-battery line sold worldwide under the Battery-Box brand (Premium/HVS/HVM/LVS families). Premium HVS stacks 2–5 modules for 5.1–12.8 kWh usable (to 38.4 kWh with 3 parallel); Premium HVM stacks 3–8 modules for 8.3–22.1 kWh (to 66.2 kWh parallel). Plug-in tower design with no internal wiring; inverter-agnostic — certified with Fronius, GoodWe, Kostal, SMA, SolarEdge and others; VDE 2510-50 safety standard, 96% efficiency, IP55, 10-year warranty. Kept BYD a top-3 global residential storage supplier in 2025 (InfoLink, behind Tesla and Huawei).
productsAndServices.positioning: Unlike Tesla Powerwall (integrated AC battery) and Huawei LUNA (paired with Huawei inverters), Battery-Box is a DC battery sold inverter-agnostic through the installer channel — the 'works with everything' option in European/Australian rooftop solar
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Solar distribution channel and installer networks (notably Europe/Australia); certified inverter-partner ecosystem
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Residential rooftop solar self-consumption and backup; small commercial via LVS/HVM stacking

productsAndServices.name: EV platform (adjacent volume engine)
productsAndServices.description: The automotive group is the scale engine that funds Blade cell cost curves: 4.60M NEVs sold in 2025 (>1M exported). Key platforms: Super e-Platform (March 2025) — first mass-produced full-domain 1,000 V architecture with 10C 'flash charging' at up to 1 MW (400 km range in 5 min; Han L / Tang L first), backed by liquid-cooled 1,360 kW charging terminals; e-Platform 3.0 / 3.0 Evo — 800 V architecture with 8-in-1 integrated drive; 5th-gen DM-i hybrid (May 2024) — 46.06% engine thermal efficiency, as low as 2.9 L/100 km at low charge, ~2,100 km combined range; and the 2nd-generation Blade Battery (March 2026) — 10–70% charge in 5 minutes, reported 190–210 Wh/kg. The storage business reorganized in August 2025 into Domestic and Overseas centers (Europe, MEA, Asia-Pacific); the 2025–26 China EV price war remains the group's dominant margin story.
highlights: Same Blade LFP cell platform and FinDreams supply chain shared between vehicles and storage — EV volume underwrites storage-cell cost leadership
productsAndServices.positioning: vs Tesla: BYD out-ships it in NEVs and (per Benchmark) in BESS; vs CATL: BYD is its own anchor cell customer, so storage pricing rides on EV-scale amortization
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Company-owned dealer networks and distributors in 110+ markets
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Global mass-market EV/PHEV buyers; the flash-charging station buildout (thousands planned in China) is a captive demand source for storage-buffered charging

recentDevelopments.headline: H1 2026: revenue RMB 344.82B (-7.13%), net profit RMB 12.33B (-20.54%); Q2 net profit RMB 8.2B (+29.8%), the first quarterly growth in five quarters; overseas revenue above half of the total for the first time
recentDevelopments.read: The half fell and the quarter turned. Overseas revenue at 52.57% of the total is the structural change; the profit decline is domestic price war plus foreign-exchange pressure. Every listed Chinese BESS peer grew profit sharply in the same half, which is the measure of how much of BYD storage is masked by an auto P&L moving the other way.

recentDevelopments.headline: Benchmark places BYD #1 in H1 2026 BESS system-integrator shipments at 9.1% of 313 GWh and #4 in cells at 6.7% of 490 GWh; InfoLink also ranks BYD #1 in systems
recentDevelopments.read: Two independent rankers agree on the integrator crown for the half — the cleanest storage claim in the file, and one that survives BYD disclosing no storage revenue.

recentDevelopments.headline: 11.275 GWh HaoHan contract signed with Masdar for Abu Dhabi's 5.2 GW / 19 GWh round-the-clock RTC project
recentDevelopments.read: HaoHan validated at gigascale within a year of launch — BYD supplies the majority of the world's first gigascale solar+storage RTC plant (online 2027).

recentDevelopments.headline: Greenvolt signs BYD Energy for Siedlce, 600 MW / 2.4 GWh — Poland’s largest BESS, construction from Q3 2026
recentDevelopments.read: Europe joins the Middle East and Latin America as a named HaoHan market; the non-China storage book is where BYD’s storage growth is visible while the domestic auto business compresses.

recentDevelopments.headline: Up to BRL 500M ($98M) BESS production line planned in Brazil — module/pack/system integration, not cells
recentDevelopments.read: Localizing system assembly ahead of Brazil's first large industrial storage auction (Dec 2026) — the SEC/Grenergy playbook of following tender demand with local content.

recentDevelopments.headline: Added to the Department of War §1260H list of Chinese military companies; BYD rejects the designation in a voluntary HKEX announcement the next day
recentDevelopments.read: Procurement screening rather than a sales ban: §805 bars DoD contracting with a listed entity from 30 June 2026 and reaches goods produced by one from 30 June 2027. BYD says it is neither a military company nor a military-civil fusion contributor and notes the list is not a sanctions regime. It compounds the §154 statutory naming already running to October 2027.

recentDevelopments.headline: Benchmark ranks BYD the #1 global BESS integrator for 2025 (>60 GWh shipped, 13% share), overtaking Tesla (46.7 GWh)
recentDevelopments.read: The scale crown is real but scope-dependent — InfoLink's system ranking still places BYD #3; either way BYD now leads or podiums every storage league table.

recentDevelopments.headline: Brazil adds BYD to the forced-labour "dirty list" over 2024 conditions at the Camaçari site
recentDevelopments.read: Blocks government loans and triggers private-bank credit review in the market where BYD is building a US$98M BESS line for the December 2026 capacity auctions. A separate R$257m labour suit remains unresolved.

recentDevelopments.headline: Grenergy locks in 2.6 GWh of MC Cube-T for its Central Oasis platform in Chile
recentDevelopments.read: Third repeat purchase from the same customer (after 3 GWh + 3.5 GWh at Oasis de Atacama) — the strongest possible field-performance endorsement of MC Cube-T in Latin America.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2nd-generation Blade Battery unveiled: 10–70% charge in 5 minutes, ~97% in 9 minutes, reported 190–210 Wh/kg
recentDevelopments.read: EV-side cell breakthrough that historically cascades into the storage cell family — chemistry reports conflict (LMFP vs improved LFP), so treat density figures as provisional.

recentDevelopments.headline: HaoHan platform launched: 14.5 MWh single DC block (world's largest), 2,710 Ah long Blade cell, GC Flux grid-forming PCS
recentDevelopments.read: BYD leapfrogs the 6–8 MWh container race entirely — betting that block size, land efficiency and in-house grid-forming decide the next tender cycle.

recentDevelopments.headline: 3.5 GWh MC Cube-T supply deal for phase 6 of Grenergy's Oasis de Atacama (624 units) — Latin America's largest battery supply deal at signing
recentDevelopments.read: Chile becomes BYD's LatAm showcase: 6.5 GWh cumulative with one developer on an 11 GWh project pipeline.

recentDevelopments.headline: Chess Plus C&I cabinet launched (233 kWh/125 kW China; 350.1 kWh US version)
recentDevelopments.read: A serious C&I re-entry led by the blade-cell safety story — fire-resistant casing and aerosol suppression aimed at the segment's thermal-incident anxiety.

recentDevelopments.headline: Super e-Platform unveiled: 1,000 V architecture, 10C flash charging at up to 1 MW — 400 km of range in 5 minutes
recentDevelopments.read: Charging-speed leadership as the new EV battleground; the flash-charging station network (with storage buffering) creates captive demand for BYD's own BESS.

recentDevelopments.headline: 12.5 GWh grid-scale BESS contract with Saudi Electricity Company (5 × 500 MW/2,500 MWh) — world's largest grid-side award at signing
recentDevelopments.read: Anchor reference for MC Cube-T at national-utility scale; lifts cumulative SEC cooperation to 15.1 GWh.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess BYD's storage cost position derives from vertical integration and the Blade LFP platform shared with its NEV business — planned cell capacity above 500 GWh amortizes across vehicles and storage. Basis: company capacity disclosures and filings.

(High confidence) We assess BYD leads H1 2026 BESS system-integrator shipments, and (Moderate confidence) that the FY2025 crown is genuinely disputed rather than merely scope-dependent. For the half, two independent rankers agree: Benchmark puts BYD first at 9.1% of 313 GWh and InfoLink also ranks it first, calling BYD and Sungrow 'extremely similar' in utility-scale. For the full year 2025 the rankers split — Benchmark says BYD #1 at 60 GWh and 13%, while Wood Mackenzie and InfoLink both say Tesla #1, Sungrow #2, BYD #3. Wood Mackenzie's own two 2025 instruments also differ (BYD #3 on market share, #4 on the ten-criteria scorecard), which is a difference of instrument rather than a contradiction but reads as one if cited side by side without the basis. Basis: none of the rankers states its metric precisely enough — shipments versus installations versus contracted volume is never nailed down — and no source reconciles them. In cells BYD is consistently #4 (SNE 35.7 GWh / 7.7%; Benchmark 6.7%), and even there SNE's volume and Benchmark's implied volume differ by about 3 GWh. Never cite a single ranking as settled.

(High confidence) We assess BYD's storage performance is structurally invisible in its own accounts and will stay that way. The H1 2026 interim disclosed no standalone energy-storage revenue line, as no prior period has: storage sits inside 'automobiles and related products'. The consequence is that BYD is excluded from like-for-like interim comparisons of listed Chinese BESS players — the August 2026 Energy-Storage.News review of CATL, EVE, CALB, Gotion, Great Power, REPT and Desay does not mention BYD at all — while every one of those peers grew net profit sharply in the same half and BYD's group profit fell 20.54%. Basis: the disclosure record and the peer review. Any BESS revenue figure attributed to BYD is a third-party estimate; only shipment volumes and ranks exist.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the HaoHan/Masdar RTC award and three repeat MC Cube-T purchases from the same Chilean developer indicate field-performance credibility at gigascale; the 2027 delivery schedule is the verification point.
(Moderate confidence) We assess Latin America is the template for BYD's non-China storage growth — following tender demand with local assembly (Brazil) mirrors the Chile SEC/Grenergy sequence.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the regulatory fence around BYD is now three-layered and asymmetric, and that the sharpest near-term item is not American. In the US, statutory naming in NDAA §154(b) bars DoD procurement from October 2027 and the June 2026 §1260H listing brings §805 contracting bars from June 2026 and June 2027 — both procurement instruments, neither an import ban, and BYD is verified absent from the UFLPA Entity List. Whether BYD is a specified foreign entity for §45X/§48E purposes is unresolved and recorded as unresolved. In Brazil — the market BYD is building a US$98M BESS line for ahead of the December 2026 capacity auctions — BYD sits on the forced-labour 'dirty list' from April 2026, which blocks government loans and triggers bank credit review, with an R$257m labour suit unresolved. Basis: the legal-alert record and Brazilian state sources.

relationships.note: Cell customer AND head-on BESS rival: FinDreams supplies LFP cells to Tesla's Shanghai Megafactory while BYD's systems business overtook Tesla in Benchmark's 2025 integrator ranking.
relationships.context: From Q1 2025 FinDreams Battery supplies LFP cells to Tesla's Shanghai Megafactory, reportedly securing >20% of Megapack cell orders alongside primary supplier CATL — while at system level Benchmark ranked BYD the #1 global BESS integrator for 2025 (>60 GWh shipped, 13% share) over Tesla's 46.7 GWh. The duality is the point: BYD monetizes its rival's demand at the cell layer and fights it at the container layer, with HaoHan's 14.5 MWh single block against Megapack 3's ~5 MWh standardization.

relationships.note: Competes with CATL both as cell merchant and as system vendor — HaoHan 14.5 MWh vs TENER 6.25 MWh, Blade LFP vs CATL cells at the same Tesla account.
relationships.context: BYD's vertical integration is the differentiator: it consumes its own cells in vehicles and BESS at volumes that fund the cost curve, then sells the surplus merchant — meeting CATL in EV packs, storage containers, sodium-ion (MC Cube-SIB vs Naxtra) and even inside Tesla's Shanghai Megafactory supply chain, where CATL is primary supplier and FinDreams reportedly took >20%.

relationships.note: Head-on grid-forming AC-block rivalry — HaoHan's bundled GC Flux grid-forming against Sungrow's PowerTitan integrated approach; also meet in C&I (Chess Plus vs PowerStack).

Merchant-cell rival — the dossier groups Hithium with EVE and REPT BATTERO against BYD's captive-plus-merchant model. The distinction is captive consumption, not product scope: REPT BATTERO in particular also sells complete containerised systems, so 'merchant-only' is accurate about its lack of an in-house end product and inaccurate if read as cells-only.
C&I storage rival — Chess Plus competes with Sinexcel's cabinets in the segment where thermal-incident history drives procurement.
Sixth globally in storage cell shipments at 31.4 GWh and 6.8% for H1 2026, against BYD's fourth at 35.7 GWh and 7.7% — the closest competitor to BYD in that ranking.
relationships.context: The structural difference is captive demand rather than product scope. BYD consumes its own cells in its own vehicles and systems; REPT BATTERO has no in-house end product, but it does sell complete containerised systems as well as bare cells, so it is not a cells-only supplier.
relationships.source: SNE Research H1 2026 storage cell shipment ranking

policyExposure.regime: NDAA §154 Department of Defense procurement ban
policyExposure.exposure: BYD Company, Ltd. is one of exactly six entities named in §154(b) of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act, alongside CATL, Envision Energy, EVE Energy, Gotion High-tech and Hithium. From 1 October 2027 the Department of Defense may not procure batteries produced by any of them, where 'produced by' means the entity assembled or manufactured the final product or created or provided a majority of the components. A Secretary of Defense waiver exists. The ban is prospective and confined to Defense procurement — it is not a government-wide bar.
policyExposure.mitigation: None available — statutory naming is not curable by restructuring.

policyExposure.exposure: BYD Company Limited was added to the §1260H list in the update released 8 June 2026 — 65 additions taking the list to 188 entities — on military-civil fusion grounds. The consequence runs through §805 of the FY2024 NDAA in two phases: from 30 June 2026 the Department may not enter, renew or extend contracts with a listed entity, and from 30 June 2027 that bar extends to goods and services produced or developed by one. A §1260H designation is not itself a sanction and imposes no import ban or prohibition on commercial transactions; the DFARS rule implementing §805 has not been published. BYD responded the next day in a voluntary HKEX announcement, stating that it is neither a Chinese military company nor a military-civil fusion contributor and that there is no justification for its inclusion, noting that the list is not a sanctions list and does not restrict securities transactions, and reserving the right to seek review or legal proceedings. That response is the company's own and is recorded as such, not as adjudication.
policyExposure.mitigation: None at entity level; the company disputes the designation on the record. The practical effect on BYD is procurement screening by federal-adjacent and utility buyers rather than a direct sales bar.

policyExposure.exposure: UNRESOLVED, AND RECORDED AS SUCH. A US storage project using BYD systems must clear a material assistance cost ratio of 55% non-prohibited content in 2026, rising toward 75% by 2030, with construction started before 1 January 2026 exempt; Treasury and IRS issued Notice 2026-15 in February 2026. Whether BYD is itself a specified foreign entity is the open question. No fetched primary or law-firm document names BYD as an SFE. What is established is that BYD is named in NDAA §154(b), and that counsel describe the SFE definition as importing entities on certain national-security lists — including, per one summary, entities ineligible for Department of Defense contracts — without enumerating which lists or naming companies. The final link is therefore an inference, not a verified fact, and the document most likely to settle it was unreachable from this session's egress. Treat as a well-supported inference with a documented gap.
policyExposure.mitigation: Not determinable until the SFE question is closed against Notice 2026-15 itself.

policyExposure.exposure: Recorded because the corpus and the trade press both tend to assume the opposite. BYD Company Limited, BYD Auto, FinDreams and BYD Electronic do not appear on the DHS UFLPA Entity List as of the 31 July 2026 update, which added 43 companies effective 3 August and took the list to roughly 285 entities. No automotive OEM is on that list. Verified against the DHS list itself, not against coverage of it.
policyExposure.mitigation: Not applicable — this is an absence rather than an exposure.

policyExposure.regime: Brazil forced-labour registry and labour prosecution
policyExposure.exposure: BYD was added to Brazil's 'dirty list' of employers in April 2026 over conditions at the Camaçari site in 2024, where 471 Chinese workers were brought in illegally and 163 were rescued from conditions the authorities characterised as slavery-like. Listing blocks access to government loans and triggers credit review at private banks; it does not halt plant operations. A separate R$257m (~US$50m) suit filed by Bahia labour prosecutors in May 2025 against BYD and two contractors was unresolved as of this revision. This is the clearest non-US policy exposure in the file and it bears on the market BYD is building a BESS line for.
policyExposure.mitigation: Not established from the public record.
